title: LoRA: Fine-Tuning Through a Low-Rank Window
summary: Freeze the pretrained weights and learn only a low-rank update ΔW = (α/r)·BA: why it works, why B starts at zero, how the gradients flow, and how merging gives zero-overhead inference.
takeaways: LoRA freezes W and trains ΔW = (α/r)·BA with r ≪ d, often under 1% of the parameters.
B starts at zero, so the adapted model starts identical to the pretrained one. A starts random so gradients can flow.
W gets no gradient and no optimizer state. That is where the memory savings come from.
Merging W + ΔW after training gives a plain linear layer, so inference has no extra cost.

steps.label: Freeze
steps.detail: Keep the pretrained W fixed: no gradients, no optimizer state.

steps.label: Attach
steps.detail: Add A (r × d_in, random) and B (d_out × r, zeros) next to W.

steps.label: Forward
steps.detail: h = xWᵀ + (α/r)(xAᵀ)Bᵀ. At step 0 this equals the base model.

steps.label: Train A, B
steps.detail: Backprop only into A and B with the usual optimizer.

steps.label: Merge or swap
steps.detail: Fold ΔW into W for deployment, or keep small per-task adapters.

terms.definition: Adapting a pretrained model by training a small set of new or selected parameters while the rest stay frozen.
The inner dimension of B·A. It caps the rank of the update and sets the adapter's size.
A constant multiplier on BA that keeps the update size comparable when r changes.
The smallest number of free parameters needed to reach a given fraction of full-training quality.
Replacing W with W + (α/r)BA after training, so inference uses one ordinary matrix.
